note: WHICH HOUSE, REALM AND PLACE THE ARCHIVE MAY PUT A DEVICE ON, and for every other one the measured reason its corner stays bare. C20 ruled a heraldic device into the top outer corner of every leaf; C36 ruled that it inherits from house and realm. Before this table 124 of 582 routes resolved a device -- 0 of them through the house field, 0 of 91 places, 3 of 60 realms -- so 916 of 1,164 corners were bare and NOTHING SAID WHY. A blank here is a finding, not a gap: it carries the count of corpus passages that name the subject beside blazon language and still attribute nothing to it.
rule: [C] the corpus names the charge AS a device, emblem, banner, badge, sign or standard OF this subject. [I-H] the corpus attests the image for the subject but not as heraldry, or attests it for the parent of a branch this archive's own genealogy declares. [I-M]/[I-L] longer or weaker chains. [EXT] third-party scholarship -- none today. There is no other kind, and [NEO] is deliberately absent: this dataset may not invent a device. A [C] may rest only on a tier-1 source, or a tier-2 source carrying Tolkien's own words -- the test arda_sources.json states in its own tier note, which turns on whose words they are and not on the editor's framing.
